_metadata.description: Significant screen-hit lists from 7 published genome-wide CRISPR host-factor screens for SARS-CoV-2. Each hit is a gene that passed the paper's own significance threshold and is traceable to a specific supplementary table or main figure. Extracted directly from each paper's supplementary hit tables (6 via PubMed Central / Europe PMC open-access supplements; Baggen via Springer publisher supplement).
_metadata.direction_convention: proviral = knockout/knockdown REDUCES infection (dependency factor); antiviral = knockout INCREASES infection (restriction factor). For CRISPR-activation (GOF) hits (Biering antiviral set only), 'antiviral' means OVEREXPRESSION reduces infection; flagged per-hit.
_metadata.gene_symbols: Current official HGNC symbols (verified via rest.genenames.org, 2026). 28 hit records had a previous/alias symbol updated to the current one, with the original retained in 'original_symbol' and an 'hgnc_note'. Separately, Daniloski's duplicate CTSL/CTSL1 library rows were merged into one CTSL hit (hgnc_note only, no original_symbol). Monkey (Chlorocebus) LOC gene models from the Vero-E6 screen and one withdrawn HGNC entry (SPHAR) are flagged rather than remapped.
_metadata.no_fabrication: Every hit is sourced to a specific table/figure. No genes were inferred from abstracts or discussion text.

Wei et al. (Cell 2021).hit_source: Table S1 (mmc1), sheet 'VeroE6 SARS-2 genomewide zscore'; hit set reproduces Fig 2B (top 25 resistance + top 25 sensitization ranked by mean Cas9-v2 z-score)
Wei et al. (Cell 2021).threshold: Paper calls hits by gene-level FDR (Fisher's method across 5 Cas9-v2 conditions + Benjamini-Hochberg on averaged z-scores). Supplement provides per-condition z-scores only, not FDR; the reproducible paper-defined hit set is the top-25-per-direction shown in Fig 2B, ranked by 'Cas9-v2 Avg.' z-score.
Wei et al. (Cell 2021).coverage: top/high-confidence hits only: top 25 proviral (resistance, highest +z) + top 25 antiviral (sensitization, lowest -z). Full genome-wide FDR list not provided in supplement.
Wei et al. (Cell 2021).completeness_note: Complete for the paper's displayed hit set. The supplement (Table S1) provides only per-condition z-scores for all ~21,672 genes, not the gene-level FDR the paper uses to formally call hits, so a fully reproducible genome-wide FDR list is not extractable. The reported set is the paper's own Fig 2B hit set: top 25 resistance (proviral) + top 25 sensitization (antiviral) ranked by mean Cas9-v2 z-score. Key anchors (ACE2, SMARCA4, CTSL, DYRK1A up; HIRA, CABIN1 down) reproduce exactly. Three monkey (Chlorocebus) LOC gene models in the proviral top-25 have no clean human ortholog and are flagged.

Daniloski et al. (Cell 2021).completeness_note: Complete and reproducible. Full genome-wide MAGeCK hit list extracted at the stringent FDR<0.05 in either MOI condition (28 unique genes after merging a duplicate CTSL/CTSL1 library row). Positive-selection screen, so all hits are proviral; there is no antiviral arm. Paper also discusses looser sets (top-50 overlap, RRA p<0.05 ~1000 genes) available in the same table if a broader cut is wanted.

Schneider et al. (Cell 2021).hit_source: Table S1A (mmc1), sheet 'Table_S1A' — Huh-7.5 37 C SARS-CoV-2 genome-wide screen (Brunello library, MAGeCK); genes with the supplement's own 'Sig' flag
Schneider et al. (Cell 2021).threshold: FDR < 0.05 (MAGeCK-derived gene-wise fitness score). Direction by z-score sign: z>0 = proviral (candidate host/dependency factor), z<0 = antiviral (candidate restriction factor). Paper text states 84 proviral + 62 antiviral = 146 at 37C; the supplement 'Sig' flag marks 147 (84 proviral + 63 antiviral), one antiviral gene at FDR~0.048 on the boundary.
Schneider et al. (Cell 2021).coverage: full genome-wide significant-hit list (all Sig-flagged genes, both directions) for the primary 37C SARS-CoV-2 screen.
Schneider et al. (Cell 2021).completeness_note: Complete and fully reproducible. The supplement carries the paper's own 'Sig' hit flag; 147 flagged genes in the primary Huh-7.5 37C SARS-CoV-2 screen (84 proviral z>0, 63 antiviral z<0) at FDR<0.05. Matches the paper's stated 146 (84+62) within one boundary antiviral gene at FDR~0.048. TMEM41B and GAG/SREBP pathway hits present as expected.

_optional_accessory_ORF_orthology_check.description: Orthology of SARS-CoV-2 accessory ORFs in SARS-CoV-1 (Sarbecovirus, closely related) vs MERS-CoV (Merbecovirus, distinct lineage). Accessory genes are NOT conserved across betacoronavirus lineages/genera; MERS carries a completely different accessory complement (ORF3, 4a, 4b, 5).
sources: Established comparative-genomics consensus on betacoronavirus accessory-gene complements: SARS-CoV-2 encodes accessory ORFs 3a,6,7a,7b,8,9b (+debated 3b,9c,10); SARS-CoV-1 encodes 3a,3b,6,7a,7b,8a,8b,9b (+9c/ORF14); MERS-CoV encodes a DISTINCT set ORF3,4a,4b,5 with no orthologs of the SARS accessory ORFs.

SARS-CoV-2-specific / divergence details (ORF10 absent in SARS-CoV-1; ORF3b full-length in SARS-CoV-1 but truncated ~22aa in SARS-CoV-2; ORF8 orthologous locus but <20% aa identity, split into 8a/8b in SARS-CoV-1 via a 29-nt deletion) are standard sarbecovirus findings.

Further reading (titles surfaced via web search; full text not verified in-session, treat as pointers not quoted evidence): 'SARS-CoV-2 ORF8 accessory protein is a virulence factor' (PMC10653805); 'Variability of Accessory Proteins Rules the SARS-CoV-2 Pathogenicity' (bioRxiv 2020.11.06.372227); 'Hidden players of COVID-19: evolving roles of SARS-CoV-2 accessory proteins' (PMC12698434).

Orf3a.note: Clear ortholog in SARS-CoV-1 (~72% aa identity). No true ortholog in MERS (MERS accessory set is 3/4a/4b/5).

Orf3b.note: Positionally orthologous ORF3b locus exists in SARS-CoV-1 as the canonical full-length protein; in SARS-CoV-2 ORF3b is severely truncated by a premature stop (~22 aa), so the functional full-length form is a SARS-CoV-1 feature. No MERS ortholog.

Orf6.note: Ortholog present in SARS-CoV-1. No MERS ortholog.

Orf7a.note: Ortholog present in SARS-CoV-1. No MERS ortholog.

Orf7b.note: (Not in the user's list, included for completeness.) Ortholog present in SARS-CoV-1. No MERS ortholog.

Orf8.note: Orthologous locus in SARS-CoV-1 but <20% aa identity; in SARS-CoV-1 a 29-nt deletion during 2002-03 human transmission split orf8 into orf8a/orf8b (early civet isolates had single orf8/orf8ab). No MERS ortholog.

Orf9b.note: Ortholog present in SARS-CoV-1 (overlaps N gene). No MERS ortholog.

Orf9c.note: Positionally orthologous ORF9c/ORF14 locus exists in SARS-CoV-1; expression/protein-coding status debated in both viruses. No MERS ortholog.

Orf10.note: SARS-CoV-2-specific: no ORF10 ortholog in SARS-CoV-1. No MERS ortholog. (Coding status of SARS-CoV-2 ORF10 itself is debated.)

_optional_accessory_ORF_orthology_check.summary: Among the 8 SARS-CoV-2 accessory ORFs checked, 7 (Orf3a, Orf3b, Orf6, Orf7a, Orf8, Orf9b, Orf9c) have a positional ortholog in SARS-CoV-1 and only Orf10 is SARS-CoV-2-specific with no SARS-CoV-1 ortholog. NONE of the SARS-CoV-2 accessory ORFs have a true ortholog in MERS-CoV, which carries a distinct accessory complement (ORF3, ORF4a, ORF4b, ORF5). This corroborates the user's 'MERS has ORF3/4a/4b/5, no SARS accessory ORFs' rule.
